title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 1.10 of the May 1966 letter to Tate. S is a scheme of characteristic p > 0, and crystals are taken 'absolutely', i.e. relative to R = Spec Z. Grothendieck notes that Spec Z_p would give the same thing, because p is nilpotent on every infinitesimal thickening of a characteristic-p scheme.

(i) Let M be a crystal of modules of finite presentation on S and s a point of S. Let s' be the spectrum of a perfect closure of k(s). By 1.5, the infinitesimal thickenings of a perfect field are pro-represented by the truncated Witt vectors W_n(k(s')). So M(s') becomes a compatible system of W_n-modules, i.e. a finitely generated W(k(s'))-module.

(ii) Hence a crystal on S is proposed as the formalization of an 'algebraic family' of modules over the Witt rings at the perfect points over S. Grothendieck adds that the notion is finer than this and should also give the right notion of family when S is not perfect, e.g. the spectrum of a function field.

(iii) The extra structure for 'algebraic families of Dieudonné modules' comes from the absolute Frobenius frob_S : S -> S. It acts on crystals of any species F by pull-back, M^(p) = frob_S^*(M). A p-crystal is a crystal M together with a morphism F : M^(p) -> M; this is the modern F-crystal.

(iv) p-crystals of a given species form a category. It depends functorially on F under covariant cartesian functors of fibred categories. This gives the covariant tensor operations: tensor products, exterior and symmetric powers.

(v) Duality reverses arrows. This leads to p^{-1}-crystals, i.e. a crystal with V : M -> M^(p). The next page goes on to bicrystals / Dieudonné crystals with FV = p and VF = p, bicrystals of weight i, the Tate bicrystal, and isocrystals obtained by tensoring the Hom with Q.

The problem served is to build a theory of crystalline (de Rham-type) cohomology in characteristic p whose H^1 recovers Dieudonné theory of p-divisible groups and formal groups in families.
errors: The equivalence 'cristal de présentation finie gives a module of finite type over W(k(s'))' implicitly passes to the limit over the W_n. It needs the compatible system to consist of finitely presented W_n-modules (Mittag-Leffler / finite-type limit). This is harmless but unstated.

The crystals here are on the infinitesimal site, without divided powers. Grothendieck later recognized that divided powers are needed for the good theory in characteristic p (crystalline site, Berthelot). For perfect points this does not matter, but the hope that the notion 'gives the right notion of family' for non-perfect S really requires the PD version.
The next page writes VF = id_{M^(p)} for weight 1 (it should be p·id). That error is not on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known 1966 letter to Tate, which founded crystalline cohomology. The definitions on this page (absolute crystals, F-crystals, V for duality) entered the literature through Grothendieck's own 1968 and 1970 texts and the work of Berthelot, Mazur and Katz. Nothing here is unrecorded.
transcription_corrections: 's'x est le spectre' — typed 's'' with an overstruck character; read 's' est le spectre'.
The formula is typed 'frob_S (M)' with no visible asterisk; the transcription's frob_S^* is the intended meaning.

In 'les p-cristaux sur S d'espèce F donnée', the handwritten 'sur S' is inserted and only 'd'espèce' appears struck. 'F donnée' seems to remain, as the sequel 'dépendant fonctoriellement de F' requires.
'tensoriel(s)' was typed with an overstrike; 'intrcduite' should read 'introduire'; 'une notions duale' is a typo in the original for 'une notion duale'.
